description:
Parent: fz-kdt

## Goal

Preserve movement direction when one publisher withdraws a contribution from a
multi-publisher cumulative fact. If the joined value changes but other
publishers keep the fact present, every reader must wake with `shift=true` and
rebase before replacing any evidence derived from the old, wider value.

fz-kdt.64 remains gated on this invariant. This ticket fixes classification
only; it must not enable new `AnalyzeActivation` withdrawal or change
`conclude_preserving_frontier`.

## Current defect

`ActivationInputs` is cumulative (`FactKey::is_cumulative`). Its contribution
store correctly removes one publisher and recomputes the surviving aggregate.
When that removal changes the aggregate while another publisher remains,
`FactTable::replace_outputs` reports a present-to-present revision bump.

`Scheduler::dispatch_changes` then reconstructs movement direction only from:

- whether the whole fact disappeared;
- whether the completing job was already rebased; and
- whether the key is replacing rather than cumulative.

For a non-rebased publisher withdrawing one contribution from a still-present
`ActivationInputs` fact, those observations produce `shift=false`. The reader
therefore joins its next result as though the input grew, although its ground
narrowed.

This is already representable in the current tree:
`compiler2_activation_inputs_retract_one_publishers_stale_contribution`
withdraws `SeedRoot`'s row, leaves another publisher's row standing, advances
the revision, and narrows the joined value. The test has no reader and therefore
does not assert the missing ground-shift propagation.

Telemetry cannot repair the loss: `work_graph.applied.wakes[].shift` serializes
the scheduler's boolean, and `CausalReport::shifts.shift_wakes` counts that
field.

## Law

A changed removal from a join is a descent even when the fact remains present.
Revision topology is insufficient to distinguish it from an ascent:

- cumulative upsert changing `Some(n)` to `Some(n+1)`: ascent;
- changed publisher withdrawal leaving other publishers,
  `Some(n)` to `Some(n+1)`: ground shift;
- last contentful publisher withdrawal, `Some(n)` to `None`: ground shift;
- equal withdrawal: no content movement and no content wake.

The point that knows whether the changed key was omitted/withdrawn must carry
that provenance to dispatch. Do not infer direction from revision numbers.

## Strategy

1. Extend the fact-change path so a changed withdrawal of a publisher's claim
   remains distinguishable from an ordinary cumulative upsert through
   `FactTable::replace_outputs` and scheduler dispatch.
2. Classify that movement as a ground shift while preserving the existing
   classifications for cumulative ascents, bottom presence changes, replacing
   changes, whole-fact retractions, and changes emitted by rebased publishers.
3. Keep wake telemetry derived from the scheduler's authoritative
   classification; expose any added movement field in the public applied-step
   schema only if it is required to make the classification auditable without
   a subscriber.
4. Update `fact-engine.md` to name changed withdrawal from a still-present
   cumulative aggregate as a ground shift.
5. Keep fz-kdt.64 dependent on this ticket. Any later ticket that enables
   `AnalyzeActivation` value replacement or withdrawal must separately provide
   a termination argument addressing fz-kdt.106's refuted budget-cliff
   ping-pong prototypes.

## Red-first tests

- Scheduler altitude: create a cumulative fact with two publishers and a
  current reader; withdraw one publisher while marking the still-present joined
  fact changed. Assert:
  - old and new revisions are both present;
  - the reader wakes;
  - the matching wake has `shift=true`;
  - the reader is rebased.
- World altitude: extend the existing `ActivationInputs` two-publisher
  withdrawal case with a reader. Assert the surviving row/value, the
  present-to-present revision bump, and the shifted wake together.
- Sibling guards:
  - adding or widening a cumulative contribution remains `shift=false`;
  - an equal withdrawal emits no content wake;
  - last-publisher contentful retraction remains `shift=true`;
  - present-at-bottom appearance/retraction remains non-content movement.

## Acceptance

- All red-first tests pass.
- `work_graph.applied.wakes[].shift` is true for the changed
  multi-publisher-withdrawal case, and causal aggregation counts that shifted
  wake.
- Existing cumulative-ascent, bottom-presence, replacing-change, retraction,
  derivation-scoping, settlement, and determinism tests remain green.
- Full library, CLI, and fixture-matrix gates pass.
- Existing fixture shift/rebase telemetry pins either remain unchanged or every
  movement is explained as an already-reachable misclassified withdrawal.
- No new withdrawal path, preservation change, value-level replacement, or
  decommission behavior lands in this ticket.

comments.text: RIDER (fz-kdt.106 landed, a010532e8, 2026-09-01): still open and still gating fz-kdt.64. Note 106's prototype record: mid-drive value-level replace (narrowing) on ActivationInputs was twice refuted by non-settlement -- the grow-only property is load-bearing for termination. Any route that enables withdrawal must carry a termination argument, not just correct shift classification.

title: A changed withdrawal from a still-present cumulative fact must propagate as a ground shift
